IEAGHG (2017). Understanding the Cost of Retrofitting CO2 capture in an Integrated Oil Refinery. Technical Review 2017-TR8, August 2017. IEA Greenhouse Gas R&D Programme, Cheltenham, UK (IEAGHG manager John Gale; ReCAP project run by SINTEF Energy Research with Amec Foster Wheeler, CONCAWE, Gassnova/CLIMIT). Compiles: SINTEF Energy Research report 2017:00220 Performance analysis of CO2 capture options (Anantharaman, Jordal, Fu, Wahl, Vagenes; 2017-06-20); SINTEF report 2017:00222 cost of retrofitting CO2 capture (final, 2017-06-23; ISBN 978-82-14-06683-8; authors not printed on the text pages); Amec Foster Wheeler Description of Reference Plants, doc BD0839A-PR-0000-RE-001 rev F01 2016-09-16; Amec FW Constructability Assessment (rev C00 2017-05-30). Web: https://www.sintef.no/globalassets/project/recap/2017-tr8-recap-project.pdf

Targeted pass over the 320-page compilation (PDF pp.1-320). LOCATORS: every reference gives the PDF page and the printed page of the sub-report: Cost report 2017:00222 printed p = PDF p - 190 (PDF 196-291); Performance report 2017:00220 printed p = PDF p - 142 (PDF 143-190); Reference plants (Amec FW) page = PDF p - 13 (PDF 16-141). LOADED: (1) all 16 MEA post-combustion capture cases (Base Cases 1-4 = hydroskimming 100 kbbl/d, medium conversion 220, high conversion 220, high conversion 350 kbbl/d): per case the capture-and-compression section (capture-unit_amine: total plant cost, fixed/variable opex, specific reboiler steam, electricity, 90% capture rate, cooling water, MEA make-up) and, separately, the whole retrofit (capture-unit_amine_retrofit-total: capex, opex, abatement cost $/tCO2 avoided), both parsed from Appendix D and cross-checked (sections sum to totals; Table 5/7/9/11 $/t values agree). (2) per-source absorber equipment costs (Table 3-31: NGCC, POW, SMR, FCC, CDU/VDU, CRF absorbers). (3) refinery-integrated SMR with and without flue-gas capture (Perf. Table 22) and host rows for FCC, fired heaters, SMR, POW; oxy-FCC pilot literature review (Sect. 9, Table 23, reprinted from de Mello 2013). (4) the four reference refineries (CO2 per t crude printed; fuel per t crude DERIVED from Gcal/h x 8,400 h / crude kt/y), per-unit CO2, fuel-combustion CO2 factors, per-unit utility consumptions (Table 4-7) and hydrogen consumptions (Table 4-5). NOT LOADED: Appendix A equipment lists (sizes only), Appendix B cost laws (kept as scaling exponents in other-values), sensitivity charts (no printed numbers), charts read-off, constructability study (no numbers), IEAGHG 2017/02 SMR tables 14/15/21 (separate source ieaghg_2017_smr-merchant-hydrogen-ccs), Excel model (not in the PDF). CASE DESIGN: costs exist only per CASE (mixes of sources), never per source, except the single-source cases (01-01, 02-01, 03-01, 04-01 = power plant; 04-04 = SMR) and the Table 3-31 absorber sections; FCC-only, heater-only and CHP-only capture costs therefore cannot be isolated. COST BASIS: all costs are retrofit costs in Q4 2015 US dollars (Cost report p.30); the capex row is total plant cost (installed + 15% project contingency); total capital requirement (adds spare parts, start-up, owner cost, interest during construction) is in other-values. Abatement cost = (annualised capex + opex)/CO2 AVOIDED, 25 y, 8%, 96% utilisation, excludes transport and storage; avoided is only about 60% of captured because the new gas-fired CHP plant emits uncaptured CO2.

(1) Cost report Table 16 and Section 3 label k$ amounts as k EUR and print 151.4 EUR/tCO2 for case 04-04, but Appendix D (same capex 503,664) gives 162.1 $/tCO2; Appendix D used. Table 15 is headed corrected to US dollars but equals Table 14 EUR x CEPCI only. (2) The Cost report labels the specific reboiler duty "per tCO2,avoided" (Tables 6/8/10/12) while the Performance report gives the same figure per t CO2 CAPTURED; specific power also differs (e.g. case 04-03: 162 vs 146.5 kWh/t); Performance-report values loaded. (3) Base Case 4 total CO2: Reference-plants Table 8-6 gives 398.8 t/h (SMR process CO2 29.7 t/h) but the capture reports use 466.7 t/h (SMR 117.3 t/h, Table 18); the case shares (71.7% captured in 04-03) follow the latter. (4) Table 4-7 gives delayed coking zero fuel while Tables 7-7/8-7 burn 4.4-6.0 t/h fuel gas in the coker. (5) Table 4-11 (SMR syngas) has a garbled duplicated composition column. (6) Appendix D prints decimal commas for cases 01-03 and 04-05 (185,3; 162,2). (7) Constructability study and IEAGHG overview duplicate the reports; no extra numbers.
